Updated ballot count places Kristen Sneddon ahead in mayoral race

The City College professor ran a campaign that prioritized affordability and climate resilience
Logan Rae Fleming, News Editor
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 1:25
Instaread
November 10, 2026
Michael Lopez
File photo, mayoral candidate Kristen Sneddon speaks to a reporter at an election night watch party Nov. 3 at Validation Ale in Santa Barbara, Calif. Sneddon trailed closely behind opponent Eric Friedman’s vote count throughout election night.

Kristen Sneddon now leads the City of Santa Barbara’s mayoral race by 296 votes ahead of opponent Eric Friedman, who had led the preliminary vote count since election night. 

When The Channels spoke with Sneddon on the morning of Nov. 4, she made no mention of a concession.

Sneddon noted that there were still many uncounted votes, and attributed the closeness of the race to both her and Friedman being left-leaning candidates. 

“We’ve seen across the county and locally that democrats are in really positive positions,” Sneddon said. “I think any time when you have democrats running in the same race it is going to be close.”

She also expressed support for incoming City Council members Devin Wardlow, Ian Buacke and Gabe Escobedo. 

“Your vote really matters, and the City Council is going to be in good hands with the district council members who were elected,” Sneddon said.  

Sneddon, the current City Council member for district 4, and a geology professor at City College, emphasized affordability and climate resilience in her campaign. At City College’s mayoral forum she expressed that would not pursue taxes that would negatively affect the welfare of college students. 

According to the County of Santa Barbara’s elections website there are 22,276 ballots still left to be counted for this race. Updates to the count are posted to the website at 3 p.m. every Tuesday and Thursday until election results are certified.
